questions.question: Due to an increase of 20 percent in the price of rice, the consumer decreases his consumption by 5 percent. What is the percentage change in total expenditure?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Increase in price = 20%

Decrease in consumption = 5%

**Concept:**

Percentage change in expenditure = Percentage change in price - Percentage change in consumption - (Percentage change in price × Percentage change in consumption) / 100

**Solution:**

Percentage change in expenditure = 20% - 5% - (20% × 5%)/100

15% - 1% = 14%

**Therefore, the percentage change in total expenditure is 14%.**

questions.question: If a + b = 3 and ab = 2, then what is the value of 2a³ + 2b³?
questions.solution:
**Given**

a + b = 3

ab = 2

**Concept:**

This is the formula to simplify cubic expressions: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)

**Solution:**

2a³ + 2b³ = 2(a³ + b³)

2(a + b)(a² - ab + b²) (Substituting from given)

2(3)(a² - 2 + b²) (as a + b = 3 and ab = 2)

2(3)(a² + b² - 2) (as a² + b² = (a + b)² - 2ab = 9 - 4 = 5)

2(3)(5 - 2) = 2(3)(3) = 18

**fore, the value of 2a³ + 2b³ is 18.**

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral A B C D, ∠A is opposite to ∠C. If ∠A = 110 degree, then what is the value of ∠C?
questions.solution:
**Given**

∠A = 110°

**Concept:**

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary (i.e., they add up to 180°).

**Solution:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58008a715d2fd95d7f5ad61b5b0c030b261ce5f55920c848f930113277e2ceeb.png] 

∠C = 180° - ∠A

∠C = 180° - 110° = 70°

**Therefore, the value of ∠C is 70°.**

questions.question: If P+(1)/(P)=5, then what is the value of P³+(1)/(P³)?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P + 1/P = 5

**Concept:**

Cubic equation formula from quadratic equation: If P + 1/P = n, then P³ + 1/P³ = n³ - 3n

**Solution:**

P³ + 1/P³ = 5³ - 3×5

P³ + 1/P³ = 125 - 15 = 110

**The value of P³ + 1/P³ is 110.**

questions.question: Selling price of a watch is Rs. 1056 and profit percentage is 10 percent. If selling price is Rs. 800 , then what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Selling Price (SP1) = Rs. 1056

Profit % = 10%

New Selling Price (SP2) = Rs. 800

**Concept:**

Profit and loss are calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

**Solution:**

Find the Cost Price (CP) using the first set of information: CP = SP1 / (1 + Profit%) = Rs. 1056 / (1 + 10/100) = Rs. 960

Find the loss% using the second set of information: Loss% = ((CP - SP2) / CP) × 100 = ((960 - 800) / 960) × 100 = 16.67%

**Hence, the loss percentage will be 16.67%.**

The pie chart given below show the runs scored by 5 batsmen in a cricket match. Total runs scored by these batsmen are 300 . Runs scored by a batsman is shown as a percentage of runs scored by all these five batsmen.

What is the average runs scored in F, I and J?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Percentage of runs for F = 18%, I = 24%, J = 6%; Total runs = 300

**Concept:**

The average of a quantity is the sum of all quantities divided by the number of quantities.

**Solution:**

Calculate runs for F, I, and J: F = 18% of 300 = 54, I = 24% of 300 = 72, J = 6% of 300 = 18

Calculate average: (F + I + J)/3 = (54 + 72 + 18)/3 = 48

**Hence, the average runs scored in F, I and J is 48**

questions.question: The length of a cuboid is thrice of its breadth and the height of cuboid is twice of its breadth. If the breadth of the cuboid is 6 cm. then what is the total surface area of cuboid?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Breadth (b) = 6 cm

Length (l) = 3b = 18 cm

Height (h) = 2b = 12 cm

**Concept:**

The total surface area of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

**Solution:**

Substitute the values into the formula:

2(18 × 6 + 6 × 12 + 12 × 18)

2(108 + 72 + 216) = 792 cm²

**Hence, the total surface area of the cuboid is 792 cm².**

questions.question: If A = a cosec θ + b cot θ and B = a cot θ + b cosec θ, then what is the value of A² - B²?
questions.solution:
**Given**

A = a cosec θ + b cot θ

B = a cot θ + b cosec θ

**Concept:**

A trigonometric identity can be used here: cosec² θ - cot² θ = 1

**Solution:**

Substitute the given values into the formula: A² - B² = (a² - b²)(cosec² θ - cot² θ) = (a² - b²) × 1 = a² - b²

**Hence, the value of A² - B² is a² - b².**

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a work alone in 12,15 and 20 days respectively. They started the work together. P left the work 8 days before the work was completed and Q left the work 5 days after P had left. R completed the remaining work alone. How many days will be required to complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can complete the work in 12 days.

Q can complete the work in 15 days.

R can complete the work in 20 days.

P left the work 8 days before it was completed.

Q left the work 5 days after P had left.

R completed the remaining work alone.

**Concept:**

The total work done by individuals working together is equal to the sum of their individual work done in the same time.

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60

Efficiency of P = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of Q = 60/15 = 4

Efficiency of R = 60/20 = 3

Let the total work done in t days.

According to question,

⇒ 5(t - 8) + 4(t - 3) + 3t = 60

⇒ 5t - 40 + 4t - 12 + 3t = 60

⇒ 12t = 112

⇒ t = 112/12 = 28/3 days

**∴ 28/3 days will be required to complete the whole work.**

questions.question: A bus starts from a bus stand after every 50 minutes in the same direction. Mohit is walking in opposite direction with a speed of 50 km/hr. If Mohit meets each bus in 10 minutes, then what is the speed of bus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The distance covered by the bus in (50 − 10) = 40 minutes is equal to the distance covered by Mohit in 10 minutes.

Since the distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time.

Ratio of Time (Bus : Mohit) = 40 : 10 = 4 : 1

Ratio of Speed (Bus : Mohit) = 1 : 4

Mohit's speed = 4 units ⇒ 50 km/hr, so Bus's speed = 1 unit ⇒ 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Bus frequency time = 50 mins

Mohit's meeting time with each bus = 10 mins

Mohit's speed = 50 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

 
• Next Bus Mohit Meet in 10 mins 
 
 Bus travels for 10 mins Mohit travels for 10 mins 
• 
• 
• Initial Gap = Bus Speed × 50 mins 
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the bus be V km/hr.

⇒ Distance between two consecutive buses = V × (50/60) km

⇒ Relative speed of Bus and Mohit = (V + 50) km/hr

⇒ Time taken to meet = 10/60 hours

We know, Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ 10/60 = [V × (50/60)] ÷ (V + 50)

⇒ 1/6 = (5V/6) ÷ (V + 50)

⇒ (V + 50) / 6 = 5V / 6

⇒ V + 50 = 5V

⇒ 4V = 50

⇒ V = 12.5

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance in Periodic Events

If a bus or train departs periodically after every T interval, the constant distance maintained between any two consecutive vehicles on the route is D = Speed × T.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 150 percent of the cost price. If 20 percent discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Marked price is 150% of the cost price

Discount given is 20%

**Concept:**

Profit percentage is calculated as (Selling price - Cost price)/Cost price × 100%

**Solution:**

Selling price after discount = 150% - 20% of 150% = 150% - 30% = 120%

Profit percentage = (Selling price - Cost price)/Cost price × 100% = (120% - 100%)/100% × 100% = 20%

**Therefore, the profit percentage is 20%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**MP/CP = (100 + profit%)/(100 - loss%)

150/100 = (100 + p)/80 ⇒ P = 120 -100 = 20%

questions.question: An amount of Rs.12,029 is divided among P, Q and R such that P's share is 5 times Q's share and R's share is one-third of P's share. What is the share of R?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total amount = Rs. 12,029

P's share = 5Q

R's share = P/3

**Concept:**

The total amount is the sum of the shares of P, Q, and R.

**Solution:**

Express all shares in terms of Q: P = 5Q, R = 5Q/3

Total = P + Q + R = 5Q + Q + 5Q/3 = 12,029

Solving the above equation we get Q = Rs. 1569

Therefore, R's share = 5Q/3 = 5 × 1569/3 = Rs. 2615

**Therefore, the share of R is Rs. 2615.**

questions.question: Sum of the angles made by a chord at the centre and on the major arc of a circle is 225 degree. What will be the angle made at the major arc of this circle?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Sum of the angles at the center and major arc = 225 degrees

**Concept**

 In a circle, the angle at the center is twice the angle subtended by the same chord at the major arc.

**Solution:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c8c83ff55af596e9703d7b332d2c3bf6644064d11ebb913562e592037ec1adc.png] 

Let the angle at the center be 2x and the angle at the major arc be x

2x + x = 225

Solving the above equation, we get x = 75 degrees

**Therefore, the angle made at the major arc of this circle is 75 degrees.**

questions.question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 7 matches is 49 and in other 9 matches the average is 27. What is the average runs scored by the batsman in these 16 matches?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average runs in 7 matches = 49

Average runs in 9 matches = 27

**Concept:**

The total average is the sum of all runs divided by the total number of matches.

**Solution:**

Total runs in 7 matches = 7 × 49 = 343

Total runs in 9 matches = 9 × 27 = 243

Total runs in 16 matches = 343 + 243 = 586

Average runs in 16 matches = 586/16 = 36.625

**Therefore, the average runs scored by the batsman in these 16 matches is 36.625.**
